parts.text:
2
Three of these quantities have the same unit.
Which quantity has a different unit?
energy
A
distance
B
force
C
power × time
D
rate of change of momentum

hints: Write the SI unit for each word in the question: energy in joules $\text{J}$, distance in metres $\text{m}$, force in newtons $\text{N}$, power in watts $\text{W}$, momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Connect energy to force using work done $W = F \times d$, and connect force to momentum using $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, to see what unit energy/distance and rate of change of momentum must give.
Connect power to energy using $P = E / t$, so rearrange to find what power $\times$ time represents and check whether its joule unit matches the newton unit of the other three.
walkthrough: Recall the SI units: energy is joule $\text{J}$, power is watt $\text{W} = \text{J s}^{-1}$, force is newton $\text{N} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, and momentum is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
For energy divided by distance, use $work = force \times distance$, so $force = energy / distance$. The unit is $\text{J m}^{-1} = \text{N}$.

For force and for rate of change of momentum, use Newton's second law $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$. Momentum change per second has unit $\text{kg m s}^{-1} / \text{s} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} = \text{N}$, so both have the newton unit.
For power $\times$ time, use $P = E / t$, so $E = P \times t$. The unit is $\text{W} \times \text{s} = (\text{J s}^{-1}) \times \text{s} = \text{J}$.
Three quantities give the newton $\text{N}$ and only power $\times$ time gives the joule $\text{J}$ of energy. This is option C

A.explanation: Energy has unit joule $\text{J}$ and distance has unit metre $\text{m}$, so $\text{J m}^{-1}$ is the newton $\text{N}$, the same as force.

B.explanation: Force has SI unit newton $\text{N}$, which matches energy divided by distance and rate of change of momentum.

C.explanation: Power is energy per time in watts, so power $\times$ time gives $(\text{J s}^{-1}) \times \text{s} = \text{J}$, the joule of energy, different from the newton.

D.explanation: From $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, rate of change of momentum has unit $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is the newton $\text{N}$.
